items.followUp: Define a heteroatomic molecule and give one example.

rubric.why: A homoatomic molecule contains atoms of the same element.
rubric.description: Defines a homoatomic molecule as one made up of atoms of the same element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its atoms are of the same element or kind.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a homoatomic molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example, such as H₂ or O₂.

modelAnswer: A homoatomic molecule is a molecule made up of atoms of the same element.

items.followUp: Define ionization energy and give one example.

rubric.why: Electron affinity is the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom gains an electron.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity in terms of energy released when a neutral gaseous atom accepts an electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy-release definition, including a gaseous atom gaining an electron.

rubric.why: The example must show chlorine accepting an electron to form a negative ion.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of chlorine gaining an electron to form a chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct example or reaction.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
For example, a chlorine atom accepts an electron: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g).
